MODE_DECISIONS: Guardian mode: Approve with strict guardrails. Finance is most determinative. Recommends proceeding only after all compliance requirements are fully satisfied and vendor exit clause is contractually guaranteed. Emphasizes cost containment with 20% contingency buffer and quarterly financial reviews. Accepts slower timeline to minimize downside exposure. Pioneer mode: Approve with accelerated timeline. Technology is most determinative. Recommends fast-tracking vendor selection and compressing pilot phase to 6 weeks to capture first-mover advantage. Prioritizes innovation velocity and talent attraction benefits. Accepts higher short-term risk for faster competitive positioning. Architect mode: Approve with phased approach. Operations is most determinative. Recommends balanced execution with clear phase gates between vendor selection, pilot, and rollout. Weighs cross-domain dependencies equally and builds consensus checkpoints into the timeline. Optimizes for organizational alignment and execution reliability.
CONVERGENCE_POINTS: All three modes approve the cloud migration initiative -- no mode recommends rejection or indefinite deferral. All three modes require vendor evaluation as a prerequisite step before committing to implementation, agreeing that vendor selection quality is critical to long-term success.
DIVERGENCE_POINTS: Timeline urgency: Pioneer compresses to 8 months while Guardian extends to 16 months and Architect targets 12 months. The 8-month spread reflects fundamentally different risk appetites. Risk tolerance threshold: Guardian requires all risks mitigated before proceeding, Pioneer accepts calculated risks for speed, and Architect accepts risks with monitoring guardrails. This produces different go/no-go criteria at each phase gate.
KEY_CHOICE: The underlying decision is speed of transformation versus risk containment. Pioneer optimizes for competitive advantage and innovation velocity at the cost of higher execution risk. Guardian optimizes for downside protection and regulatory certainty at the cost of slower time-to-value. Architect seeks a middle path that balances both but may satisfy neither fully.
MODE_SENSITIVITY: Medium -- all modes agree on direction (approve migration) but differ meaningfully on scope, timeline, and risk acceptance thresholds
